headline_stat.name: directionally tuned units / mean tuning strength

stated_limitation: individual units show correlations near zero (mean: 0.010). This suggests that motor cortex prioritizes direction encoding over speed encoding at the single-trial level, though population-level speed signals may emerge through other mechanisms.

justification.dataset: 000129 is a real motor-cortex reaching dataset where directional tuning exists, but it is a continuous random-target task mislabeled as center-out, making it a defensible but non-obvious choice.
justification.handling: Real data streamed from S3, but velocity is never scaled by dt (mislabeled m/s), behavioral rate is hardcoded at 30 Hz, no unit quality filtering, and whole-trial velocity averaging is questionable for this paradigm.
justification.analysis: No shuffle or null control for directional tuning and a modulation-depth metric that is positive by construction, so the central 'all units tuned' claim rests on no significance test.
justification.correctness: Reported numbers reproduce from the code, but the interpretation is internally inconsistent (0.61 modulation-depth described as '60% modulation' and preferred directions called uniform when the figure is skewed).
justification.figures: Figures are readable but do not make the case: polar curves are noisy, and the preferred-direction-sorted heatmap shows no diagonal population structure the text claims it reveals.
justification.honesty: The write-up states preferred directions are uniformly distributed and continuously arranged when its own figures 2 and 6 show neither, presenting a noisy, unvalidated direction result as clean, which caps this axis at 1.
